title: Register Price Adjustment for Frequent Retail OTC Use — Retail Pharmacy Pricing Clause
content:
**Pharmacy Benefit, over-the-counter allowance at retail pharmacies.** The register price adjustment reduces the receipt allowance charge of a posted retail register receipt: the charge is multiplied by one minus the adjustment, within the product and before the charge is limited to the allowance balance and rounded.

**Clause.** The register price adjustment is five percent (0.05) where 3 or more retail receipts were posted on the coverage in the last six whole months, two percent (0.02) where one or two were, and nothing where none were.

**Definition.** A date falls in the last six whole months when fewer than six whole calendar months have passed from that date to today, a month counting as whole only once today's day of the month has reached that date's day of the month.

The receipts counted are the retail pharmacy purchases on the member's pharmacy coverage that carry a posting date within the last six whole months. A transmitted receipt that is not yet posted carries no posting date and is not counted.

### Adjustment table

| Retail receipts posted in the last six whole months | Register price adjustment | Charge multiplied by |
|---|---|---|
| 3 or more | 5 percent | 0.95 |
| 1 or 2 | 2 percent | 0.98 |
| None | Nothing | 1 |

### Cases (hypothetical)

- Two retail receipts posted in the last six whole months and one transmitted receipt awaiting posting: two are counted, 2 percent.
- Four retail receipts posted, one of them seven whole months ago: three are counted, 5 percent.
